placementQuiz.q: Effective cache size affects planner by:
options: Determining actual RAM allocated to PostgreSQL
Estimating how much data fits in OS cache (influences index vs seq scan choice)

blocks.md: Partitioning = physical split, logical unity. Large table becomes many small tables. Planner prunes partitions automatically. Maintenance (VACUUM, indexes) per partition.

blocks.label: range partitioning (PostgreSQL 11+)
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL 8.0+ partitioning
CREATE TABLE measurements (
  log_id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT,
  sensor_id INT NOT NULL,
  log_time DATETIME NOT NULL,
  value DECIMAL(10,2),
  PRIMARY KEY (log_id, log_time)
) PARTITION BY RANGE (UNIX_TIMESTAMP(log_time)) (
  PARTITION p202401 VALUES LESS THAN (UNIX_TIMESTAMP('2024-02-01')),
  PARTITION p202402 VALUES LESS THAN (UNIX_TIMESTAMP('2024-03-01')),
  PARTITION pmax VALUES LESS THAN MAXVALUE
);

blocks.md: **Partition pruning:** Only 2 of 12 monthly partitions scanned. Query on Jan-Feb touches only those partitions. Detach old partitions for instant archival.

items.explain: Planner only skips partitions if WHERE clause constrains the partition key (log_time in example).

items.q: Unique constraint on partitioned table requires:
options: Partition key included in unique columns
items.explain: PostgreSQL requires partition key in PRIMARY KEY / UNIQUE to enforce uniqueness within single partition.

items.q: Parallel Hash Join workers each build:
options: Full hash table on entire build side
Hash table on their partition of build side
Shared hash table in shared memory
items.explain: Each worker builds hash on its partition of build side. No shared memory — independent.

options: Gather = unordered collect; Gather Merge = ordered merge
items.explain: Gather Merge: workers return sorted data, leader merges. Gather: unordered collect.

blocks.md: **Expression must be IMMUTABLE.** No NOW(), random(), volatile functions. Expression index stores computed value — if function isn't immutable, index becomes inconsistent.

items.q: BRIN index size is ~1/30th of B-tree because:
options: Stores only min/max per block range, not every row
items.explain: BRIN summarizes 128-page ranges (default) with min/max. Tiny metadata vs per-row pointers.
Must run outside transaction. Takes share-update-exclusive lock, not exclusive.

revisionCard: Partitioning: RANGE/LIST/HASH on key; planner prunes automatically; detach for archival
BRIN for huge correlated tables (time-series); pages_per_range tunes granularity
Parallel query: Gather node, workers, cost thresholds (parallel_setup/tuple_cost)
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY — no exclusive lock; 2x space, slower build
Functional indexes for expressions (LOWER, JSONB paths); ICU collations for CI
effective_cache_size guides index vs seq scan choice; pg_stat_statements for monitoring

glossary.def: Planner excludes partitions not matching WHERE on partition key.
Column(s) used to determine which partition a row belongs to.
Multiple workers scan/process data simultaneously; leader gathers results.
BRIN parameter: how many heap pages per min/max summary. Lower = more precise, larger index.
Parallel workers return sorted data; leader merges without re-sorting.
Index built without blocking writes; takes share-update-exclusive lock.
